The MPE controller is an electrophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 542, marked as Americas / North America. It is a MIDI controller, turning key presses or touch gestures into note data that is sent to a sound module, synthesizer, sampler or sequencer for playback. A keyboard-type controller usually has a keybed, pitch and modulation wheels and pedal sockets, and can control different devices in zones; electronic music producers often use it to play software synthesizers or hardware synthesizers without a keyboard.

Inside are advanced capacitive sensing chips and sensor arrays that detect multi-touch information. On some high-end models the edges of the keyboard are covered with soft rubber or leather for comfort. The base is of solid engineering plastic or aluminium alloy. The circuit boards use PCB substrates with a high-performance microprocessor and a USB port.
